title: refactor(ci): unify lint/test/release workflows and stabilize caching
author: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Consolidate multiple GitHub Actions workflows (lint, test, and release) into a smaller set of reusable workflows to reduce maintenance burden, improve cache efficiency, and stabilize flaky jobs across the monorepo. Motivation: Over the last year we've accumulated many near-duplicate workflow files that diverged when node versions, caching strategies, and release automation were iterated on. This has caused inconsistent test behavior, longer CI times, and higher cognitive overhead when updating cross-repo standards. What I changed: - Introduced a single .github/workflows/ci.yml that handles lint, unit, and integration stages using a job matrix with explicit Node versions and runner labels. - Created .github/workflows/release.yml which uses a shared reusable workflow for release steps and dry-run checks. - Added scripts/ci/cache-helpers.sh to standardize cache keys and parallel cache restore logic (reduces cache misses under heavy CI concurrency). - Bumped actions and canonicalized to actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4 and uses node:20 by default; added matrix entry for node:18 for legacy packages. - Removed duplicated workflow fragments and updated CI documentation at docs/ci.md. - Added annotation support and a lightweight debug output for flaky test diagnosis. Checklist: - [x] Consolidate workflow files and add documentation (docs/ci.md) - [x] Standardize cache key format and restore order - [x] Keep node:18 in matrix for legacy packages - [x] Run full CI across main/branch and fix failing jobs - [x] Coordinate rollout (canary on infra/* branches for 48h) Testing & validation: - Ran full CI (lint, unit, integration) on main and a ~20-commit stress branch to validate caching under concurrency. - Observed median CI runtime reduction ~18% for lint+unit stages and cache hit rate improved from ~62% to ~86% on subsequent runs. - Performed dry-run of release job (no publish) to validate tags and changelog generation. Rollout plan: - This PR was merged to main with a short canary period: merged_at used after 48h canary where no regressions were observed. - Follow-ups: update repo templates (redwood-quickstarts) and notify SDK teams for any workflow-specific overrides. Related: ENG-2148 (CI reliability), ENG-2293 (release automation hygiene), SUP-1023 (customer incident referencing flaky CI).
commits: feat(ci): add unified ci.yml with lint/unit/integration matrix
chore(ci): add cache helpers and standardize cache keys
chore(actions): bump checkout/setup-node actions to v4
refactor(ci): extract release steps to reusable workflow and add dry-run
review_comments: Ethan Gray: Great consolidation. Two asks: (1) can we keep node:18 for any packages that still require it? (2) please add a short note about how to opt out for repos that have bespoke flows.
Maya Chen: Responded — node:18 is kept in the matrix for legacy packages; added docs/ci.md opt-out section and an example to opt out by overriding the reusable workflow.
Luis Martinez: Noticed a race in cache key generation when multiple jobs restore in parallel; suggest adding randomized suffix.
Maya Chen: Implemented a conservative restore order and atomic lock via cache-helpers to reduce collisions (see scripts/ci/cache-helpers.sh). Added tests for cache behavior in tools/ci/.
Nora Patel: CI runtimes look good. Small nit: prefer actions/setup-node cache: 'npm' for node:18 runs.
Maya Chen: Updated setup-node calls to include cache: 'npm' for node matrix entries.
release_notes: Consolidated CI workflows into unified lint/test/release pipelines; standardized cache keys and bumped GitHub Actions to v4. Expected impact: lower CI maintenance burden, faster CI runs, and more stable cache behavior.
summary: Refactor CI to unify workflows, stabilize caches, bump actions, and document opt-out patterns.
